title: Configuration resolution, validation, and consumer contracts
purpose: Find reachable parameter-contract failures from supported server configuration inputs through source selection, parsing, defaults, validation and component wiring, including persisted identity/schema guards and the boundary between node-local desired settings and Raft-applied configuration. Apply the companion evidence and ownership contract. Exclude process re-exec/recovery, lifecycle joining, operator reconciliation transitions, generic subsystem audits and performance-only tuning.
invariants: For flags bound by the production service entrypoint, explicit CLI input takes precedence over the corresponding environment variable, then the registered default. The selected environment value must parse as the declared flag type; a malformed lower-precedence environment value must not defeat an explicit valid flag. Establish special handling of environment-only inputs and custom flag types from the pinned binder and current implementation rather than assuming every environment variable follows the flag rule (deployment Configuration; main.go; cmd/server).

Absence, explicit zero, false and empty values must retain each parameter's established meaning through parsing, normalization and consumer defaults. Zero may mean disabled, unlimited, default or invalid depending on the specific parameter; derived defaults must respect explicit overrides. A value accepted at the input boundary must not silently acquire another meaning through signed/unsigned conversion, duration units, byte-size conversion, pointer omission or constructor defaults (cmd/server LoadConfig and its sentinel/default tests; consumer config comments).

Validation must enforce documented value domains and combinations on supported production entry paths before a component uses an invalid configuration. Trace the actual validators and constructor preconditions for node identity, Raft/transport settings, health hysteresis, TLS/auth combinations, snapshot sync and cluster policy; do not invent stricter ranges or equate syntactically parseable with semantically valid (bootstrap.Config.Validate and delegated validators).

A supported static operator configuration must translate from an admitted/defaulted Cluster spec to the intended server arguments and environment, preserving types, explicit values, address roles and documented extraEnv overrides. CRD defaults, operator defaults, generated environment and explicit shell arguments are separate stages, not one invented global precedence rule. This domain owns static value translation; repeated reconciliation, resource selection and rollout transitions remain operator-reconciliation-durability's responsibility.

The effective validated value must reach the intended consumer through the bootstrap module and constructor options, including distinctions between Raft and service addresses, main and read-index storage settings, and admission policy versus committed state. A wiring finding needs a supported non-default input and a concrete incorrect consumer behavior, not merely differently named fields or missing test coverage.

Normal startup must preserve the documented persisted node/cluster identity and TTL checks, with the existing explicit unsafe override limited to its established scope. Storage schema incompatibility must remain non-bypassable by that override. Missing configuration, load/decode failure, mismatch, override and restore mode are distinct paths; identify actual writes and residual bytes before claiming fail-closed behavior or an incorrect overwrite (deployment Configuration Safety Checks; bootstrap persisted_config.go/config_validation.go/module.go).

Node-local settings may influence admission or desired configuration proposals, but committed apply and replay must derive outcomes, cache effects and writes from the same committed input and replicated state. Trace desired ClusterConfig and revisioned ClusterPolicy through their proposals to applied consumers; TTL and query-checkpoint limits currently belong to replicated ClusterPolicy. Do not require equal local desired values across replicas or treat an admission-only soft limit as a strict replicated limit without an established contract (deterministic-fsm sections 3.4 and 3.6).
adversarial_questions: Which values are selected by service.Execute in the pinned go-libs version, which are read directly from the environment (such as AUTH_SCOPE_MAPPING), and which use pflag Changed or a second default? Can the same supported flag/environment input reach a different effective value because a fixture bypasses binding?

For learner-promotion-threshold, max-execution-plan-size, cache-rotation-threshold, health resume thresholds and byte-size flags, what do unset, explicit zero, false, empty, negative, overflow and malformed selected values actually mean? Can defaulting twice or unit conversion change the documented result?

Does each production path run the required validators, including normal/bootstrap/join and the intentionally separate restore mode? Can a validly parsed NaN/Inf, non-positive duration, invalid queue shape or TLS/auth combination reach a consumer outside its documented preconditions? Do not infer a range solely from the field's Go type.

After CRD admission/defaulting and operator defaults, do nil pointers and explicit zero/false retain distinct meanings in buildEnvVars? Can extraEnv replacement or an explicit argument in the generated shell command unexpectedly override the intended value? Are Raft advertise and service gRPC addresses kept distinct?

Which constructor applies a later default or receives the wrong Config field? Can a non-default setting be accepted and logged yet fail to change the intended consumer, or accidentally configure another store, endpoint or worker? Follow the consumer before declaring a no-op.

For an existing persisted record, what occurs on decode failure, identity/TTL mismatch and older/newer schema with unsafe override both off and on? Do any writes precede rejection, and which exact bytes remain? Is the asserted no-write or restore exception actually documented?

Can a local flag, environment read or version-dependent default affect processing after commit, including replay? Are the desired cache/bloom settings and desired ClusterPolicy revision/payload committed before their applied consumers use them, or can local desired state bypass the replicated value?

When local desired policy differs from applied policy, is the observed behavior an allowed admission difference, a documented policy revision rejection, or a concrete apply divergence? Does a historical example contradict the current implementation and specific contract, requiring a question rather than a bug claim?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: Run existing focused root-module tests with the pinned Nix environment: go test ./cmd/server -run '^TestLoadConfig_' and go test ./internal/bootstrap -run '^Test(Validate|HealthThresholds|ServiceAdvertiseAddr|ReconcileClusterPolicy)'. Record exact tests run; these are configuration evidence, not proof of OS re-exec or readiness.

For a proposed source-resolution reproducer, use a fresh command per case and the production binder identified through main.go and the pinned go-libs service implementation before LoadConfig. Compare default, valid environment, explicit flag over conflicting or malformed environment, and selected malformed environment across bool, integer, duration, slice and ByteSize flags. Isolate process environment; environment-mutating cases cannot use t.Parallel. Do not claim raw LoadConfig exercises service.Execute.

For a proposed consumer-wiring reproducer, pass distinct supported non-default values through LoadConfig and the actual bootstrap constructor path, capture the resulting consumer options or observable setting, and contrast unset versus explicit sentinel cases. Use existing injected listener leases if a fixture starts a server, isolated temporary stores and bounded cleanup; add no tracked reproducer during the read-only audit.

Run static operator mapping tests in their nested module: go -C misc/operator test ./internal/controller -run '^Test(BuildCommand|BuildEnvVars|ValidateClusterConfig|AppendBloomEnvVars|AppendPebbleEnvVars)'. For proposed additional cases, start from current admitted/defaulted Cluster fixtures, inspect generated args and environment with extraEnv overrides, and trace selected values through the server binder. Direct struct construction alone does not prove API reachability; no external Kubernetes mutation is authorized.

Use existing bootstrap persisted-config fixtures to inspect first boot, matching values, explicit override, both schema mismatch directions and malformed records. For proposed extra cases compare exact persisted bytes before/after validation, including any writes before rejection; do not use a same-process close/open test as evidence of crash durability or real restart recovery.

For a proposed deterministic configuration-boundary comparison, use identical committed entries and initial replicated state in isolated FSM fixtures while varying only supported local desired settings; compare outcomes, audit payloads, cache effects and writes at the same applied index. Use current ClusterPolicy processing and cluster_policy_recovery tests and rolling_config E2E as entry points, distinguishing desired-to-committed handoff from generic replay, leadership, or restart correctness. Tagged E2E requires the native test harness and its documented prerequisites.
